import Mathlib

open Finset

namespace AlignmentRationalization

universe u

theorem rational_below {x δ : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ q : ℚ, 0 ≤ (q : ℝ) ∧ (q : ℝ) ≤ x ∧ x - q < δ := by
  by_cases hzero : x = 0
  · exact ⟨0, by simp [hzero, hδ]⟩
  · have hpos : 0 < x := lt_of_le_of_ne hx (Ne.symm hzero)
    have hlow : max 0 (x - δ) < x := by
      rw [max_lt_iff]
      exact ⟨hpos, by linarith⟩
    obtain ⟨q, hqlo, hqhi⟩ := exists_rat_btwn hlow
    refine ⟨q, (le_max_left _ _).trans hqlo.le, hqhi.le, ?_⟩
    have := (le_max_right 0 (x - δ)).trans_lt hqlo
    linarith

theorem finite_rational_l1_approximation {α : Type u} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α]
    (w : α → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hsum : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ q : α → ℚ, (∀ i, 0 ≤ q i) ∧ (∑ i, q i = 1) ∧
      ∑ i, |(q i : ℝ) - w i| < ε := by
  classical
  let c : ℝ := Fintype.card α
  have hc : 0 < c := by dsimp [c]; exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_pos
  let δ : ℝ := ε / (4 * c)
  have hδ : 0 < δ := by dsimp [δ]; positivity
  have hbelow : ∀ i, ∃ q : ℚ, 0 ≤ (q : ℝ) ∧ (q : ℝ) ≤ w i ∧ w i - q < δ :=
    fun i => rational_below (hw i) hδ
  choose v hv using hbelow
  let a : α := Classical.choice inferInstance
  let S : ℚ := ∑ i, v i
  have hSreal : (S : ℝ) ≤ 1 := by
    calc
      (S : ℝ) = ∑ i, (v i : ℝ) := by simp [S]
      _ ≤ ∑ i, w i := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => (hv i).2.1
      _ = 1 := hsum
  have hS : S ≤ 1 := by exact_mod_cast hSreal
  let q : α → ℚ := fun i => v i + if i = a then 1 - S else 0
  have hqnonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ q i := by
    intro i
    have hvnonneg : 0 ≤ v i := by exact_mod_cast (hv i).1
    dsimp [q]
    split_ifs <;> linarith
  have hqsum : ∑ i, q i = 1 := by
    simp [q, Finset.sum_add_distrib, S]
  let R : ℝ := 1 - S
  have hR : 0 ≤ R := sub_nonneg.mpr hSreal
  have hRsum : R = ∑ i, (w i - (v i : ℝ)) := by
    simp [R, S, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hsum]
  have hpoint : ∀ i, |(q i : ℝ) - w i| ≤
      (w i - (v i : ℝ)) + if i = a then R else 0 := by
    intro i
    have hvle : (v i : ℝ) - w i ≤ 0 := sub_nonpos.mpr (hv i).2.1
    by_cases hi : i = a
    · have hdiff : (q i : ℝ) - w i = (v i : ℝ) - w i + R := by
        simp [q, hi, R]
        ring
      rw [hdiff]
      calc
        _ ≤ |(v i : ℝ) - w i| + |R| := abs_add_le _ _
        _ = (w i - (v i : ℝ)) + if i = a then R else 0 := by
          rw [abs_of_nonpos hvle, abs_of_nonneg hR]
          simp only [hi, ite_true]
          ring
    · simp [q, hi, abs_of_nonpos hvle]
  have herrors : ∑ i, (w i - (v i : ℝ)) ≤ c * δ := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ _i : α, δ := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => (hv i).2.2.le
      _ = c * δ := by simp [c]
  have hbudget : 2 * c * δ < ε := by
    have heq : 2 * c * δ = ε / 2 := by
      dsimp [δ]
      field_simp
      ring
    rw [heq]
    linarith
  refine ⟨q, hqnonneg, hqsum, ?_⟩
  calc
    ∑ i, |(q i : ℝ) - w i| ≤
        ∑ i, ((w i - (v i : ℝ)) + if i = a then R else 0) :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => hpoint i
    _ = (∑ i, (w i - (v i : ℝ))) + R := by simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    _ = 2 * (∑ i, (w i - (v i : ℝ))) := by rw [hRsum]; ring
    _ ≤ 2 * (c * δ) := by gcongr
    _ < ε := by nlinarith [hbudget]

theorem rationalize_uniformly {α : Type u} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α]
    (w : α → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hsum : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    {ξ η : ℝ} (hmargin : ξ < η) :
    ∃ q : α → ℚ, (∀ i, 0 ≤ q i) ∧ (∑ i, q i = 1) ∧
      ∀ b : α → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 ≤ b i ∧ b i ≤ 1) →
        (∑ i, w i * b i) ≤ ξ → (∑ i, (q i : ℝ) * b i) < η := by
  obtain ⟨q, hqnonneg, hqsum, hdist⟩ :=
    finite_rational_l1_approximation w hw hsum (sub_pos.mpr hmargin)
  refine ⟨q, hqnonneg, hqsum, ?_⟩
  intro b hb hwb
  have heq : (∑ i, (q i : ℝ) * b i) - (∑ i, w i * b i) =
      ∑ i, (((q i : ℝ) - w i) * b i) := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    ring
  have hdiff : |(∑ i, (q i : ℝ) * b i) - (∑ i, w i * b i)| < η - ξ := by
    rw [heq]
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i, |((q i : ℝ) - w i) * b i| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ i, |(q i : ℝ) - w i| := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro i _
        rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (hb i).1]
        exact mul_le_of_le_one_right (abs_nonneg _) (hb i).2
      _ < η - ξ := hdist
  have hupper := (abs_lt.mp hdiff).2
  linarith

end AlignmentRationalization

statement_fidelity.text:
# Fidelity of the rationalization formalization

The ledger claim is `A_RATIONALIZATION`. The formal source is this
directory's `Main.lean`. Unlike the three-layer source in the parent
directory, this result is not restricted to any value of `s` or `d`.

The outcome type `alpha : Type u` is arbitrary, finite, and nonempty.
For alignment it is the finite nonempty set of `s`-subsets of `[r]`,
with `r >= s`. The input `w : alpha -> Real` is any nonnegative real
probability law; `hsum` states its sum is exactly one.

`rational_below` proves that a nonnegative real number admits a
nonnegative rational approximation from below with any strictly
positive absolute tolerance. The zero case is included.

`finite_rational_l1_approximation` quantifies over every positive real
`epsilon` and produces `q : alpha -> Rat` with all coordinates
nonnegative, total mass exactly one, and

    sum i, abs ((q i : Real) - w i) < epsilon.

The proof approximates each weight from below and puts the rational
residual mass at one distinguished outcome. Normalization and
nonnegativity are conclusions, not assumptions about a proposed
approximation.

The principal declaration `rationalize_uniformly` assumes only
`xi < eta`. It produces the single rational probability law `q`
before universally quantifying over the test function `b`. For every
`b : alpha -> Real` satisfying `0 <= b i <= 1`, it proves

    sum i, w i * b i <= xi
       -> sum i, (q i : Real) * b i < eta.

Bad-set indicators are special cases of these test functions. Thus
the same `q` works for every allowed pattern and every label universe,
without enumerating or bounding those families. The strict tolerance
margin is preserved exactly.

There are no project axioms or manuscript results among the
hypotheses. The proof uses Mathlib's rational density, finite sums,
absolute-value inequalities, and rational/real field arithmetic.
It does not prove that the real sampler `w` exists. In particular it
does not certify `A_ALIGNMENT`, minimax, Ramsey homogenization, or
the invariant-cut step.
